This summer, GDC's Community Engagement Centers became hands-on classrooms during our STEM exploration days 🔍

Students learned about the work behind building a new train tunnel. With guidance from project experts, they planned and built their own model tunnels 🚆

The Gateway Development Commission will hold a virtual public Board Meeting on Monday, August 24, 2026, at 11:00 AM. Information about the meeting, including instructions on how to watch the meeting live and provide public comment, is available here: gatewayprogram.org/board-meetin...

GDC's board meeting scheduled for August 19, 2026 is canceled and will be rescheduled. Notice of a new date and time will be provided in accordance with the GDC Act and GDC Bylaws and Open Meetings Policy. Additional details will be shared on our website when they are available.

The Hudson Yards Concrete Casing - Section 3 team completed two major concrete pours in July. Over two 18-hour pours, crews placed more than 5,500 cubic yards of concrete for the roof of this section of the tunnel.

Learn more about HYCC-3 at www.gatewayprogram.org/hudson-yards...

The Gateway Development Commission will hold a virtual public Board Meeting on Wednesday, August 19, 2026, at 11:30 AM. Information about the meeting, including instructions on how to watch the meeting live and provide public comment, is available here: gatewayprogram.org/board-meetin...

"I've always wanted to teach history, and now I get to make history."

Members of @weareliuna.bsky.social Local 472 are preparing for tunnel boring at the Palisades Portal. They shared what the opportunity to work on the Hudson Tunnel Project means to them.

Our Chief of Program Delivery and Chief Engineer took CNN's Richard Quest on a tour of our construction site in the Hudson River to explain the ground stabilization work we're doing to prepare the riverbed for tunnel boring. Watch the segment to learn more about this important work!

In the 1800s, dirt and rubble were used to extend Manhattan's shoreline. To prepare for tunnel boring through this fill, we're installing pipes in Hudson River Park that will circulate cold brine underground, freezing the loose material into a solid block that is easier to tunnel through.

GDC's board meeting on July 28, 2026 is canceled and will be rescheduled. Notice of a new date and time will be provided in accordance with the GDC Act and the Commission Bylaws and Open Meetings Policy. Additional information will be shared on our website when it is available.

The Gateway Development Commission will hold a public Board Meeting on July 28, 2026, at 10:00 A.M. Registration and public comment information can be found here: www.gatewayprogram.org/board-meetin...

While the tunnel boring machines are assembled, crews are building access shafts in NY and NJ that will enable workers on the surface to support construction deep underground.

Workers are currently installing the cap beams around the top of the shaft walls. Next step: excavation.

Two years ago today, GDC signed the Full Funding Grant Agreement for the Hudson Tunnel Project. You can see the progress we've made since then on both sides of the Hudson River, and in it. We're getting the job done, and we won't stop until we deliver the reliable infrastructure riders deserve!

GDC will hold a virtual public Board Meeting tomorrow, Wednesday, July 8, 2026, at 12:00 P.M. More information, including instructions on how to watch the meeting live and provide public comment, is available here: www.gatewayprogram.org/board-meetin...

GDC will hold a virtual public Board Meeting on Wednesday, July 8, 2026, at 12:00 P.M. More information about the meeting, including instructions on how to watch the meeting live and provide public comment, is available here: www.gatewayprogram.org/board-meetin...

The Gateway Development Commission will hold a virtual public Board Meeting on Wednesday, July 8, 2026, at 12 pm. Those who would like to provide live virtual public comment or submit a written or pre-recorded statement can find additional details here: gatewayprogram.org/board-meetin...

The Hudson Tunnel Project is more than infrastructure - it's a real-world classroom.

This year, GDC partnered with schools near construction sites to use the project to teach students about science, engineering, history, and more.

We can't wait to get back into classrooms in the fall!

We don't have to wait until the new tunnel opens to benefit from the Hudson Tunnel Project. 

In a new op-ed for ROI-NJ, NJ Chamber of Commerce President & CEO Tom Bracken explains how construction is already creating jobs and supporting businesses. 
 
Read the op-ed: www.roi-nj.com/2026/06/18/o...

The Hudson Tunnel Project is back on track and building momentum.

From awarding new construction contracts to opening our second Community Engagement Center, the latest edition of our newsletter has all the updates. 

Read it here: mailchi.mp/gatewayprogr...

Curious about the Hudson Tunnel Project? Stop by one of our Community Engagement Centers in New York and New Jersey. 

Explore interactive exhibits, step inside a model of the new tunnel, and talk with GDC staff.  

Plan your visit at www.gatewayprogram.org/community-engagement.html

Our newest construction camera just went live!

Now you can see our progress building the tunnel launch box and assembling the first set of tunnel boring machines for the Hudson Tunnel Project in real time.

Check it out at www.gatewayprogram.org

The Hudson Tunnel Project keeps moving forward. 

Today we awarded the contract for the New Jersey Surface Alignment Project, which will build the infrastructure to connect the new tunnel to the existing Northeast Corridor. 

Learn more at www.gatewayprogram.org/nj-surface-a...

GDC will hold a public Board Meeting on Monday, June 1, 2026, at 10:00 am. Those who would like to participate virtually must submit written or pre-recorded video statements by 5:00 pm today via www.gatewayprogram.org/board-meetin...

GDC will hold a public Board Meeting on Monday, June 1, 2026, at 10 am. Members of the public who would like to participate virtually may submit written or pre-recorded video statements no later than Sunday, May 31, 2026, at 5 pm. Thank you to those who have already done so.

The walls of the new tunnel tubes will be made of thousands of interlocking concrete segments.

The segments for the section of the tunnel under the Palisades in New Jersey are being manufactured now at a factory in Connecticut. 

Completed segments will start shipping to New Jersey soon!

The Gateway Development Commission will hold a public Board meeting on June 1, 2026, at 10:00 A.M. Registration and public comment information can be found here: www.gatewayprogram.org/board-meetin...

Assembling tunnel boring machines is no small undertaking. Before these massive machines can begin digging, they have to be transported, delivered, and assembled.

STV, part of the Hudson Tunnel Project delivery team, explains what goes into getting these complex machines ready to launch.

🚧Construction Update🚧

The HYCC-3 Project has entered a new phase: adding the roof to the tunnel box. 

We do this by filling the tunnel with sand and pouring concrete over it, then removing the sand once the concrete hardens. The end result: a fully enclosed box trains can travel through.

Our Chief Engineer has worked on tunneling projects all over the world. Hear him explain what it takes to tunnel through the Palisades cliffs and see the progress we're making on assembling the machines that will get the job done in this new report from @nbcnewyork.com

Tunnel boring machines are massive, complex pieces of equipment, and we're building two in New Jersey! Click the link to see what it takes to assemble these complex machines and go inside the launch box where they will begin digging through the hard rock of the Palisades.

Did you know that the Palisades made of some of the hardest rock on earth? @fox5ny.bsky.social takes you behind the scenes of the work happening now to assemble our custom-built tunnel boring machines that will break through this rock. Click the link to learn more.

1910: Picks and Shovels

2026: Huge high-tech machines 

Click the link to learn more about how we'll bore the new rail tunnel under the Hudson River with machines up to the task.

Five active construction sites. Hundreds of workers. One much-needed upgrade to our rail network. 

We just added new pictures from our construction sites to our photo gallery. Click the link to see the progress we made in April.

www.gatewayprogram.org/photo-galler...

Big infrastructure project, meet the next generation 🤝

GDC's Community Engagement team recently visited two North Bergen elementary schools to teach more than 400 students about the Hudson Tunnel Project and work happening in their neighborhoods.

On International Workers' Day, GDC recognizes the skilled workforce moving the Hudson Tunnel Project forward.

This project depends on the workers on our construction sites every day. We're grateful for their role in building infrastructure that will serve the region for generations.

#MayDay

ICYMI: This week GDC awarded the contract for Hudson Tunnel Project Package 1C: The Hudson River Tunnel Section. With this award, all tunnel boring work for the new tunnel is under contract, and six of the ten HTP construction packages are underway or complete. Click the link to learn more.

The Hudson Tunnel Project is moving forward with another major milestone. We awarded the contract to build the section of the new tunnel under the Hudson River, bringing us another step closer to a new two-track tunnel connecting NJ and NY. Bloomberg has the story.

Today the Gateway Development Commission Board approved the contract for Hudson Tunnel Project Package 1C: The Hudson River Tunnel Section. Six of the 10 HTP construction packages are now in progress or complete. 

Learn more about this milestone here: www.gatewayprogram.org/wp-content/u...

GDC will hold a public Board Meeting on Monday, April 27, 2026 at 10:30 am. Those wishing to participate virtually must submit written or pre-recorded video statements by 5:00 pm today via www.gatewayprogram.org/board-meetin...

For Patrick, a shop steward with Local 825, working on the Hudson Tunnel Project has brought stability and helped him provide for his family. He and his crew take pride in building something that will benefit future generations, and they carry that sense of purpose with them every day on the job.

GDC will hold a public Board Meeting on Monday, April 27, 2026, at 10:30 am. Those wishing to participate virtually may submit written or pre-recorded video statements no later than Sunday, April 26, 2026, at 5:00 pm. Thank you to all those who have already done so.

This is what nationwide impact looks like: G & D Fab & Welding in Stark County, Ohio is building shields for some of the machines that we'll use to build the Hudson Tunnel Project.
 
Click the link to learn more about how the HTP is supporting jobs across the USA.

The Hudson Tunnel Project is creating good, long-term jobs that enable hundreds of workers to support their families. For Martin, working on the Palisades Tunnel Project provides more than just a paycheck - it offers stability and peace of mind.

The Gateway Development Commission will hold an in-person public Board Meeting on Monday, April 27, 2026, at 10:30 am. Registration and public comment information can be found here: www.gatewayprogram.org/board-meetin....

Each of the tunnel boring machines we're assembling in New Jersey consists of 96 pieces, some weighing as much as 185 tons on their own! ENR walks through the complex process of putting together these huge machines and what comes next once they're ready to launch. www.enr.com/articles/628...

Want to see what's next for the Hudson Tunnel Project? @njbiz.bsky.social takes you to the Palisades Portal construction site, where crews are assembling the tunnel boring machines that will build the first mile of the new tunnel in New Jersey.

@gothamist.com is right - there's nothing boring about the machines that will build the new train tunnel under the Hudson River. We're assembling the first two tunnel boring machines in New Jersey now. 

Learn more and see photos of the work in progress ⬇️

It's like assembling Legos, if your Legos had to be welded together and the final product was the size of a building!

@nj.com explains what goes into assembling the two tunnel boring machines that will build the first mile of the new train tunnel under the Hudson River.

A massive effort for massive machines. @spectrumnewsny1.bsky.social breaks down the process of assembling the tunnel boring machines that will break through rocks, remove debris, and construct a concrete lining for the new tunnel. 

Check it out 👇

We're making progress toward the start of tunnel boring! The two tunnel boring machines that will build the first mile of the new train tunnel into NYC are being assembled at the staging area in New Jersey now. PIX11 joined us at the construction site to see the work. www.youtube.com/watch?v=B6OI...

George has been a member of IUOE Local 825 for 25 years. Now he's leading a team working on the Palisades Tunnel Project. He and his crew are proud to show up and work hard to build one of the biggest infrastructure projects in the country.

Colin is part of a family of builders who helped make New York City what it is today. Now he's making his mark as a member of the team building the Hudson Tunnel Project. It's that sense of legacy and the pride that comes from building something lasting that drives the workforce behind this project.

For Ronald, working on the Manhattan Tunnel Project isn't just a job, it's a chance to do something important for everybody who travels into, out of, and through New York City. It's hard work - especially in the winter - but that sense of purpose, and his great coworkers, are why he loves the job.

Congratulations to GDC's Laura Colacurcio on being recognized as a Trailblazer in Transportation by City & State!
 
Laura has played a key role in many rail projects in the region. We're thrilled to have her on the team!

Learn more about Laura's work here: www.cityandstateny.com/power-lists/...

Meet Michael from Laborers Local 731. He's been working on the Manhattan Tunnel Project since the beginning. Reflecting on his journey, he says, "Think of it: You're 30-someting years old and building one of the biggest infrastructure projects. It's pretty cool."

Hundreds of construction workers are hard at work every day building the Hudson Tunnel Project. We talked with members of IUOE Local 825 working on the Palisades Tunnel Project about what this job means to them and why they're proud to be working on this once-in-a-lifetime project.

🆕📰 Out now: the Spring 2026 edition of the GDC Gazette! Catch up on the construction progress we've made so far this year, meet some of the workers building the Hudson Tunnel Project, check out our new community engagement web page, and more. 
 
Read it here: mailchi.mp/gatewayprogr...

We're continuing to make progress toward the start of tunnel boring! The main drive unit for our second tunnel boring machine arrived at the Palisades Portal construction site last night. All the components of this machine will be on site soon.

We've already done a lot in 2026! GDC Chief of Program Delivery Jim Starace gave an update on the progress we've made so far this year at our Board Meeting on Monday.

Click here to watch his presentation: youtu.be/irrRI0L2YSY?...

GDC will hold a public board meeting on Monday, March 23, 2026 at 10:30 am. Those wishing to participate virtually must submit written or pre-recorded video statements by 5 pm today via www.gatewayprogram.org/board-meetin...

GDC will hold a public board meeting on Monday, March 23, 2026, at 10:30 am. Those wishing to participate virtually may submit written or pre-recorded video statements by Sunday, March 22, 2026, no later than 5 pm. Thank you to all those who have already done so.

GDC is partnering with the communities where Hudson Tunnel Project construction is happening to make sure everyone who will benefit from the new tunnel understands the project and the work we're doing now.

Learn more about our community outreach here: www.gatewayprogram.org/community-en...

The Gateway Development Commission will hold an in-person public Board Meeting on Monday, March 23, 2026, at 10:30 am. Registration and public comment information can be found here: www.gatewayprogram.org/board-meetin....

Workers are back on the job, the construction activities that were suspended in February have resumed, and we're already hitting construction milestones again. 

Click the link to learn more and see the latest pictures of our construction sites: www.gatewayprogram.org/wp-content/u...

The Hudson Tunnel Project is a massive, complex project. To get it done, GDC has split construction into 10 distinct projects. Many of these could be called megaprojects on their own!

Watch this video to learn how 10 projects come together to make one new tunnel: www.youtube.com/watch?v=slP5...

Reliable passenger rail unlocks jobs and drives economic growth. Leaders of NAIOP's NJ and NYC chapters explain why building the Hudson Tunnel Project now is so important for riders, workers, and businesses in this op-ed for @njspotlightnews.org: www.njspotlightnews.org/2026/03/op-e...

We're pouring concrete for the third and final section of the Hudson Yards Concrete Casing! The tunnel floor is finished, and we're making progress on the walls. When it's complete, the concrete casing will connect the new tunnel to New York Penn Station.
We're almost finished installing the slurry wall for the Hudson County Access Shaft! Once that wall is complete, we'll begin excavating the 120-foot-deep shaft.

Workers are back on the job in Manhattan and in the Hudson River! We're continuing installation of the slurry wall for the 12th Avenue Access Shaft and stabilizing the riverbed to prepare for tunnel boring.

Construction is resuming at all our sites this week. At the tunnel portal in North Bergen, we're continuing construction of the launch box where the tunnel boring machines will be assembled and start tunneling. The components of the first machine are on site, ready for assembly!

Construction of the Hudson Tunnel Project is resuming! Workers who have been impacted by the construction pause are returning to our construction sites this week. 

More info here: www.gatewayprogram.org/wp-content/u...

Rudy Duarte is one of the hundreds of union workers impacted by the Hudson Tunnel Project construction pause. His message is clear: fund this urgent project now so workers like him can get back to work building the modern, reliable infrastructure America needs.

The Gateway Development Commission will hold an in-person public Board Meeting on Tuesday, February 24, 2026, at 10:00 am. Registration and public comment information can be found here: www.gatewayprogram.org/board-meetin...

"I had to let all my guys go. There's no checks coming in for them."

Guido Rivieccio, one of the shop stewards working on the Manhattan Tunnel Project, describes the real-world impact that pausing funding for the Hudson Tunnel Project had on the workers on his team this week.

Hundreds of workers should be on site building the Hudson Tunnel Project this week. Instead, we had to put up these signs at our construction sites because we still cannot access the federal funding for the project. Funding must be restored now so we can get back to work!

Pausing construction of the Hudson Tunnel Project hurts hundreds of workers. More than 200 union workers rallied at GDC's North Bergen construction site earlier this week to call for federal funding to be restored so they can get back to work.

When work pauses, paychecks stop. LIUNA General President Brent Booker explains to NJ Spotlight that withholding funding for the Hudson Tunnel Project means lost income, fewer dollars in local economies, and workers struggling to make ends meet.

The pause in federal funding for the Hudson Tunnel Project threatens the livelihoods of hundreds of workers. Local 472 member Lamont Richardson told NY1 what's at stake for his union brothers and sisters.

We've already put more than $1 billion and countless hours into construction of the Hudson Tunnel Project. We have active construction sites across New York and New Jersey, and we're ready to start tunnel boring. Funding must be restored now so we can keep building.
Stopping construction of the Hudson Tunnel Project will hurt our regional and national economy. An extended construction pause would put nearly 100,000 total jobs at risk.

Construction of the Hudson Tunnel Project will be suspended today if disbursements of federal funding obligated to the project do not resume. 

More information about the impacts of pausing construction and our ongoing efforts to restore funding here: www.gatewayprogram.org/wp-content/u...

Nearly 1,000 workers will lose their jobs immediately when construction of the Hudson Tunnel Project pauses tomorrow, and an extended pause will put many more jobs at risk.

Funding must be restored ASAP so these hardworking men and women can get back to work.

"Superstorm Sandy showed us that at any moment, we could be shut down. And if we're shut down, we're screwed."

Steve Valeira discussed the stakes of stopping construction of the Hudson Tunnel Project at our Board Meeting last week.

Watch his statement here: www.youtube.com/live/aUxLY39...

"If we don't work, we don't get paid, and playing politics does not put food on the table for us."
 
Davon Lomax shared how stopping construction will impact the thousands of men and women building the Hudson Tunnel Project.
 
Watch his statement at our Board Meeting: www.youtube.com/live/aUxLY39...

"We're already 10,000 yards plus of concrete into this job. Why waste it?"
 
At our Board Meeting, Teamster Raymond Klein highlighted the progress already made by the hundreds of workers who will lose their jobs if funding for the Hudson Tunnel Project isn't restored.

"I urge everyone involved: Please find a solution to keep this project moving. We're all depending on you."

Robert Fawcett spoke out for the workers who will lose their jobs if construction of the Hudson Tunnel Project pauses at our Board Meeting.

Watch his testimony: youtu.be/YcjFycSlEAs?...

We're ready to build! The components of the first tunnel boring machine are on site in North Bergen, ready to be assembled in the portal launch box. Federal funding disbursements must resume ASAP so we can start tunneling.

Delays like this will become more frequent - and impact more riders - the longer we rely on the North River Tunnel. We need to complete the Hudson Tunnel Project as soon as possible to deliver reliable, modern rail infrastructure that riders can count on. 

www.bloomberg.com/news/article...

"President Donald Trump, free this money up now, so I can get to work and make my neighborhood better." 

Ironworker John Mooney spoke for the hundreds of workers building the Hudson Tunnel Project at our Board Meeting. 

Watch his full testimony here: youtu.be/YcjFycSlEAs?...

The Newsday Editorial Board is right: the Hudson Tunnel Project is the most important rail project in the country, for workers, riders, and our economy. Federal funding must be restored so construction can continue. 

Read the whole editorial here: www.newsday.com/opinion/edit...

Snow and ice don't stop us. The hundreds of hardworking men and women building the Hudson Tunnel Project show up every day and endure the elements to deliver the most urgent passenger rail project in the country. Federal funding must be restored so these workers can stay on the job.

The Hudson Tunnel Project is the most urgent infrastructure project in the country - for workers, riders, and the economy - and funding must be restored now. That's the message we heard loud and clear from workers building the tunnel at our Board Meeting yesterday.
Today GDC notified our contractors that construction of the Hudson Tunnel Project will pause on February 6 if federal funding disbursements do not resume.
Major delivery in North Bergen! The main drive unit for the first tunnel boring machine has arrived at our construction site. Most of the components for this TBM are now on site.

No missed connections here! We recently broke through the bulkhead separating the part of the Hudson Yards Concrete Casing being built under the High Line from the section that is already complete. We're now one step closer to connecting the new tunnel under the Hudson River to Penn Station.

The Gateway Development Commission will hold an in-person public Board Meeting on Tuesday, January 27, 2026, at 10:00 am. Registration and public comment information can be found here: www.gatewayprogram.org/board-meetin....

We're more than halfway finished installing the slurry wall for the Hudson County Access Shaft. This underground concrete wall will support the sides of the shaft during excavation.

Learn more and see our progress on our live construction camera at www.gatewayprogram.org/palisades-tu...

We're continuing to make progress toward the start of tunnel boring! While our tunnel boring machines are in transit from the factory, our team in New Jersey has been hard at work building the portal launch box at the foot of the Palisades. Next step: assembling the TBMs on site!

New year, new look. We just installed a fence wrap around our construction site on 12th Avenue. You can see the work happening here, and at our other sites in Manhattan, from the High Line near Hudson Yards. We also have live feeds of all five active construction sites at www.gatewayprogram.org

Last week, the HYCC-3 team completed a second major concrete pour. We poured more than 2,700 cubic yards of concrete for a section of the "invert slab," the floor of the tunnel box.

Learn more about the HYCC-3 Project at www.gatewayprogram.org/hudson-yards...

We made a lot of progress in 2025!

We manufactured our first two tunnel boring machines, opened the passage under Tonnelle Ave, passed the halfway point on HYCC-3, and much more. 

Click the link to see the latest pictures from our construction sites: www.gatewayprogram.org/photo-galler...
